body.title: Proposal: Add 'tea deploy-keys' command for repository deploy key management
body.body:
# Proposal: Manage repository deploy keys via `tea deploy-keys`

**Filed at:** https://gitea.com/gitea/tea/issues/new
**Issue title:** `Proposal: Add 'tea deploy-keys' command for repository deploy key management`
**Labels:** `kind/feature`, `kind/proposal`

---

## Motivation

`tea` currently exposes commands for most repository resources (issues, pulls, labels, milestones, releases, webhooks, branches, secrets), but **repository deploy keys have no CLI support**. Operators managing CI runners and deploy bots currently have to use the web UI or hand-craft curl calls to the Gitea API to rotate deploy keys, which is friction-prone and unauditable.

This proposal adds a top-level `tea deploy-keys` command, mirroring the shape and conventions of the existing `tea webhooks` command.

## Proposed commands

Following the `tea <noun> <verb> [<noun>] [<flags>]` convention from `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The default action of `tea deploy-keys` (no subcommand) is `list`; passing a key ID prints that key's details (analogous to `tea webhooks <id>`).

```
tea deploy-keys list [--fingerprint <fp>] [--page N] [--limit N]
tea deploy-keys create <title> [--key <inline> | --key-file <path>] [--read-only | --read-write]
tea deploy-keys delete <key-id> [--confirm|-y]
tea deploy-keys <key-id>                  # default action: show details of one key
```

Aliases: `tea deploy-keys` → `dk`, `deploy-key`. Subcommand aliases: `list` → `ls`; `create` → `add`, `c`; `delete` → `rm`.

### Flag conventions (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`)

- All subcommands inherit `--repo`, `--remote`, `--login`, `--output` from `flags.AllDefaultFlags`.
- `list` adds `--page`, `--limit` (pagination) and `--fingerprint` (filter).
- `create` accepts the key material via exactly one of `--key` (inline string) or `--key-file` (path). The two flags are mutually exclusive. `--read-only` defaults to true (matches Gitea safe-default and matches "restricting to read-only" wording in flag help).
- `delete` requires `--confirm`/`-y` to skip the "are you sure? [y/N]" prompt, identical to `tea webhooks delete`.

## Gitea API mapping

All endpoints are already exposed by the existing SDK (`code.gitea.io/sdk/gitea v0.23.2`), so **no SDK or dependency changes** are required:

| tea subcommand | HTTP                                                | SDK method                                    |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `list`         | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys`                    | `client.ListDeployKeys`                       |
| `create`       | `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys`                   | `client.CreateDeployKey`                      |
| `delete`       | `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys/{id}`            | `client.DeleteDeployKey`                      |
| default `<id>` | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys/{id}`               | `client.GetDeployKey`                         |

> The Gitea API has **no `PUT`/`PATCH` endpoint** for deploy keys, so "change a key" must be `delete` + `create`. This is documented in the `create` description and CHANGELOG; no `update` subcommand is added.

## Example usage

```
tea deploy-keys list
tea deploy-keys list --fingerprint SHA256:abc...
tea deploy-keys create CI --key-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --read-write
tea deploy-keys create backup-bot --key "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."
tea deploy-keys 7
tea deploy-keys delete 7 --confirm
```

## Output

`tea deploy-keys list` prints a table with columns: `ID`, `Title`, `Fingerprint`, `Read-Only`, `Created` — consistent with `tea webhooks list`. Supports `--output table|csv|tsv|yaml|json|simple`.

`tea deploy-keys <id>` prints markdown-style details (ID, Title, KeyID, Fingerprint, ReadOnly, Created, URL). The key material itself is **not** echoed back to stdout.

## Scope / out of scope

In scope:
- Per-repo deploy keys via the four operations above.
- Pagination and fingerprint filtering on list.

Out of scope:
- Org- or global-scope deploy keys (the Gitea API does not expose them).
- An `update`/`edit` subcommand (no API endpoint).
- User-account SSH public keys (those live under `tea admin user keys`, which is a different resource).

## Implementation sketch

- New `cmd/deploykeys/{list,create,delete}.go` (package `deploykeys`) following the `tea webhooks` layout.
- New `cmd/deploy_keys.go` at `cmd/` root registering `CmdDeployKeys` under `catEntities`, with a default action that routes to `runDeployKeyDetail` for one-key lookup.
- New `modules/print/deploy_key.go` exporting `DeployKeysList(keys, output)` and `DeployKeyDetails(key)`.
- Unit tests mirroring `cmd/webhooks/*_test.go`: command metadata, flag wiring, parsing/confirmation logic, options construction. No live API calls.
- `cmd/cmd.go`: add `&CmdDeployKeys` to the command list.
- Regenerate `docs/CLI.md` via `make docs`.

## Verification checklist

- [x] `make fmt` clean
- [x] `make test` passes (new package `code.gitea.io/tea/cmd/deploykeys` plus `modules/print` additions)
- [x] `make lint` reports 0 issues
- [x] `make docs` regenerates `docs/CLI.md`; `make docs-check` passes
- [x] `make build` produces a `tea` binary; `tea deploy-keys --help` and all subcommand helps render
- [x] Manual smoke test against a live Gitea instance (requires operator with a test repo)

## References

- CONTRIBUTING.md → "Discuss your design" — proposal-before-PR workflow.
- CONTRIBUTING.md → styleguide (`tea <noun> <verb>` shape, default = list, `delete` must prompt without `-y`).
- Gitea REST API: `repoCreateKey`, `repoDeleteKey`, `repoGetKey`, `repoListKeys` under `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys`.
- Existing analogue in tea: `cmd/webhooks/{create,delete,list,update}.go` + `cmd/webhooks.go`.

body.title: tea with extra headers for Cloudflare Zero Trust Access possible?
body.body:
Hello everyone, 

in git you can add two extra headers for Service Authentication against their Zero Trust Access policies. This allows enhanced security for gitea behind Cloudflare Zero Trust and block unauthorized access requests. 

Git has the option to add the two headers like this:
```
git config --global --add http.https://yourgitdomain/.extraHeader "CF-Access-Client-Id: CF_Service_Auth_Access"
git config --global --add http.https://yourgitdomain/.extraHeader "CF-Access-Client-Secret: CF_Service_Auth_Access_Secret"
```

So far I havent found a way to achieve this. Anyone any idea?

Thanks!
Tom

https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/service-credentials/service-tokens/
